intervals.note: Start from the SPS history page ("From late 1976 ..."), year precision with the page's wording; physics beams in the halls began later (CERN Courier dates the first North Area muons to the March 1978 commissioning run, not fetched here). End = 31 August 2026, when the SPS fell silent for Long Shutdown 3 ("CERN's injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent."); derived because the North Area is fed only by the SPS.
intervals.quote: From late 1976 the SPS started delivering proton beams to fixed-target experiments in the North and West Areas.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (injector complex)
intervals.note: Planned: the SPS is shut down for Long Shutdown 3 from 31 August 2026 (CERN, "All CERN accelerators now on the road to HiLumi"); the complex "will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards". The North Area restart date is not given separately; the SPS restart is used as a bound.
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

name: SPS North Area beams
notes: The North Area is a set of beamlines (H2, H4, H6, H8, M2, K12/P42) rather than one line; it is recorded as one beamline fed by accelerator:sps. It is not linked to experiments here (the NA experiments cite accelerator:sps): COMPASS/AMBER, NA61/SHINE, NA62, NA63, NA64 and NA65 are served, per CERN's accelerator-complex page.

Sources differ on the primary energy: the BE-EA page and the Physics Beyond Colliders report give a 400 GeV/c SPS proton beam; the SPS Operations history says "The North Area took beams of 400 and later 450 GeV, both fast- and resonant slow extracted". 400 GeV/c is recorded (current page).
Only site:cern-ecn3-north-area is listed as a detector site (NA62's cavern); EHN1 and EHN2 have no Atlas site record.

primary_beam.quote: The beams are produced after the 400 GeV/c SPS proton beam on each of the three primary targets T2, T4, and T6.

energy.note: A momentum (GeV/c) of the protons slowly extracted from the SPS onto the primary targets.
energy.quote: The beams are produced after the 400 GeV/c SPS proton beam on each of the three primary targets T2, T4, and T6.

secondary_beam.note: The page names hadron, electron and muon beams in its paragraphs on the individual beamlines (H2 to H8, M2).
secondary_beam.quote: The North Area comprises seven beamlines for secondary and tertiary beams, two experimental halls EHN1 and EHN2 above the ground as well as the underground cavern ECN3.
secondary_beam.value: secondary and tertiary hadron, electron and muon beams in seven beamlines serving the halls EHN1 and EHN2 and the cavern ECN3

proton_energy.quote: The beams are produced after the 400 GeV/c SPS proton beam on each of the three primary targets T2, T4, and T6.

summary.plain: The fixed-target beams of CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron: protons at 400 GeV/c strike three targets, and the secondary and tertiary beams that result feed the experiments in two surface halls and one underground cavern. It runs whenever the SPS does.
summary.technical: Slow-extracted 400 GeV/c SPS protons on targets T2, T4 and T6 produce seven secondary and tertiary beamlines (H2, H4, H6, H8 in EHN1; M2 to EHN2; K12/P42 to ECN3). In use since late 1976; shut down with the SPS for LS3 from 31 August 2026.
